problemStatement: The Weekly Radar archive currently writes report, rendered snapshot, receipt, and the compatibility manifest as separate atomic renames. A process interruption between those renames can leave a partial final set that is neither a committed run nor safely resumable, while retry can then be blocked or may require a second provider delivery. The existing public paths and write APIs must remain compatible.

riskAssessment.reason: The change governs durable archive visibility and retry recovery after an interruption. The design must fail closed on unverifiable residue and never claim physical atomicity across multiple public files.

acceptance: The archive writer stages report, rendered snapshot, receipt, and manifest content in a unique transaction area, then writes a date-keyed commit record last; only a complete committed record is considered a successful new run.

A prepared transaction can be deterministically recovered from its staged bytes and persisted delivery receipt without another provider send; recovery never silently overwrites a mismatched final file.

Uncommitted or unverifiable partial residue returns an explicit fail-closed error, while complete legacy archives without a transaction record remain protected as existing runs; physical cross-file atomicity is not claimed.
Same-date duplicate protection, data-branch guard, input snapshot identity/conflict behavior, retention-after-commit, public archive paths, and existing APIs remain compatible and covered by tests.
Operational/spec documentation states the logical transaction boundary, recovery path, duplicate-delivery protection, and residual production/provider limits without changing product semantics.
The complete AI Cockpit lifecycle, repository quality checks, hosted PR checks, merge, close, and clean branch/worktree audit pass for this Work Item.
guidelines: Document every new public API and keep the public archive paths and existing write API signatures compatible.
Do not add dependencies or import internal modules from other features.
Preserve the rule-only, evidence-first boundary; do not introduce Stage, Score, Ranking, Top5, investment, or capital-action behavior.
Do not claim provider or production behavior without an authorized external receipt.
Use failure injection and deterministic fixture tests rather than live Telegram or source calls.

intent.problem: The current per-file rename sequence has a crash window after Telegram delivery and before the final manifest write; a partial archive can block retry without preserving a safe archive commit point.
constraints: Keep the existing reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md, snapshots/YYYY-MM-DD.json, receipts/YYYY-MM-DD.json, weekly-radar/manifest.json paths and write_run/write_run_with_input_snapshot signatures.
Use a logical commit record and deterministic recovery; do not claim a filesystem transaction across independent public files.
Persist and reuse the delivery receipt already held by the prepared transaction; never make recovery send Telegram again.
Preserve the literal data-branch guard, input snapshot semantics, retention ordering, dry-run behavior, and provider-neutral rule-only architecture.
No live provider, Telegram, workflow, or data-branch operation may be run; verification is local, fixture-based, or hosted CI only.
intent.rationale: A prepared transaction record plus staged artifact bytes creates an auditable commit point without changing the public archive contract. Recovery can safely complete only matching content, while unverifiable residue fails closed instead of being guessed or overwritten.
